prereg.title: SEAFact-Bench extension: claim matching for social-media posts in Indonesian, Thai, Malay and Burmese

extends.note: The registered analysis is unchanged; this addendum adds a second retrieval track, evaluated after it with the same code.

prereg.data: MultiClaim v2 (Pikuliak et al., 2023), obtained from its authors under their terms of use and not redistributed: posts, fact-checks and post-fact-check pairs.

construction.fact_check_language: Detected language of the claim. A record detected as Malay or Indonesian takes the language of its publisher (Malay: semakanfakta.afp.com or a .my domain; Indonesian: cekfakta.com, tempo.co, periksafakta.afp.com, turnbackhoax.id or an .id domain); a record with both or neither keeps the detected language.
construction.post_language: A post detected as Malay or Indonesian takes the language of most of its matched fact-checks (ties: the detected language); Thai and Burmese posts must be detected as such.
construction.pairs: All three relationship types; only fact-checks in the language of the post are relevant.
construction.query_text: Post text and OCR text in the original language. Exact duplicate posts within a language are merged (earliest date, union of relevant fact-checks).
construction.document_text: Fact-check claim and title in the original language.
construction.burmese_encoding: Text with a myanmartools Zawgyi probability above 0.95 is converted to Unicode with the ICU Zawgyi-my transform.
construction.tokenization: BM25 and overlap: the registered tokenizer for Malay and Indonesian; PyThaiNLP newmm for Thai; syllable segmentation (sylbreak rules) for Burmese.
construction.split: Per language, the latest 30% of dated posts (by first appearance) form the test set; the latest 10% of the remaining dated posts form the dev set; the other posts, including undated ones, are training posts.
construction.source_queries: Up to source_query_cap training posts per language, sampled once with source_seed.
construction.subsets: Low-overlap: lowest quartile of post-to-relevant-fact-check Jaccard overlap per language (test). Novel: test posts none of whose relevant fact-checks is relevant to a training or dev post.
construction.leave_one_language_out: For each new target language, the exit heads and rankers are trained on the source queries of every other language of both tracks (SEBENARNYA-Fact, ViFactCheck, SciFact and the other new languages). Malay and Indonesian form one group: when either is the target, no Malay or Indonesian query is used for training.

hypotheses.E1: Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + BGE-M3) beats the best single retriever (chosen on dev) in macro nDCG@10 over the four new test sets.
hypotheses.E2: BGE-M3 fine-tuned on the training posts beats zero-shot BGE-M3 in nDCG@10 on the low-overlap test subset.
hypotheses.E3: Multilingual GAINER beats the score-based cascade (Current Rank) in macro nDCG@10 at B = 0.50 under leave-one-language-out training.
hypotheses.E4: Multilingual GAINER beats SEE (exit before block 0, threshold calibrated on source languages) in macro nDCG@10 at B = 0.50 under leave-one-language-out training.

tests.E1-E4: Two-sided paired sign-flip randomisation test stratified by language; statistic = macro (over languages) mean per-query difference; Holm within FE.
tests.decision: Supported if the Holm-adjusted p-value is below alpha and the effect has the hypothesised sign.

secondary: E1-E4 comparisons on the novel subset (effects and confidence intervals, unadjusted p-values).
Recall@10 and MRR@10 for every retriever; per-language results; the mMiniLM-L12 replication of E3 and E4.
prereg.not_evaluated: Verdict prediction (the matched fact-check states the verdict), abstention, and latency (candidate lists have the registered length, so the registered latency measurements apply).
